proposed_fields.description_medium: President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 13780 on March 6, 2017, replacing his January travel order. It suspended entry for 90 days for nationals of Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, subject to listed exceptions, and separately paused refugee admissions. proposed_fields.description_long: On March 6, 2017, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 13780, “Protecting the Nation from Foreign Terrorist Entry into the United States,” revising the January order. The text suspended entry for 90 days for nationals of Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, subject to stated exceptions, and separately paused refugee admissions for 120 days. Iraq was no longer among the six countries covered by the entry suspension. The order specified an effective time of March 16, 2017. These details are supported by the official Federal Register publication of the order. This correction describes the executive action itself and does not fold later district-court injunctions and appellate proceedings into one event. The supplied Associated Press URL concerns an unrelated fact-check and is not evidence for the order. Any account of the separate litigation would need citations to each order and opinion and should distinguish the Hawaii and Maryland cases from their appellate proceedings.
